source: Nievelstein, van Gog, van Dijck & Boshuizen (2013) The worked example and expertise reversal effect in less structured tasks: legal cases
finding: Human anchor. Law students studied worked examples or solved cases. Worked examples beat problem solving for novices AND advanced students. No expertise reversal.
numbers: 75 first-year and 36 third-year law students; 2x2x2 design (examples vs solving, process steps vs none, year). First-year test score: examples M=58.63 (SD 27.74) vs solving M=8.59 (SD 4.06), F(1,68)=105.2, f=1.24. Third-year: examples M=82.28 vs solving M=37.06, F(1,32)=37.03, f=1.02.
quote: worked examples were more effective for learning than problem-solving, both for novice and advanced students
limits: Short controlled session with two examples; transfer to new laws not tested. Authors say the gain may reflect legal knowledge, not reasoning skill.
agent_relevance: Even in a less structured task, a full worked case beat free problem solving. So 'open mode needs other support' does not mean 'no examples'.

source: Nievelstein, van Gog, van Dijck & Boshuizen (2013) The worked example and expertise reversal effect in less structured tasks: legal cases (process steps)
finding: A generic list of five process steps helped little on its own. Adding steps to examples added little. Steps cut first-year time on task.
numbers: First-year: process-steps main effect on test F(1,67)=4.91, p=.030, f=.24 (Welch p=.05); interaction F(1,67)=3.51, p=.065. Third-year: process steps F(1,32)<1. First-year learning-phase time: examples M=568s vs solving M=1146s (F(1,70)=58.1, f=0.75).
limits: Marginal stats. Small cells (n=9 per third-year condition).
agent_relevance: An abstract step list is weak support alone. Concrete cases carry more. Give open mode past cases, not only a procedure.

source: Renkl (2023) Using worked examples for ill-structured learning content (in Overson et al., In Their Own Words)
finding: Ill-structured content means heuristics (rules of thumb), not algorithms. Worked examples there have two content levels: the skill to learn and the topic that illustrates it. Learners must integrate both.
numbers: Cites Hilbert et al. 2004/2008: low prior knowledge of the example topic gave poor skill learning. Prompts aimed at the topic (not the skill) hurt (Schworm & Renkl 2007). Gap-filling in the topic hurt learning to prove (Hilbert 2008).
quote: In the case of worked examples for ill-structured content, there are typically two "substantial" content levels
limits: Narrative review, no pooled effect. Skills build over long periods; one lesson is a kick-off.
agent_relevance: Open-mode examples should use an easy, familiar topic and point attention to the move (the heuristic), not the topic.

source: Renkl (2023) chapter, design guidance and applications
finding: Ill-structured worked examples teach heuristic steps (support your position, add evidence, consider an alternative theory) and are paired with self-explanation prompts tied to those steps. Applications: argumentation, proof finding, legal cases, noticing in classroom video.
numbers: Three applications described; Nievelstein 2013 is the legal-case study.
limits: Narrative.
agent_relevance: A heuristic-step template plus a prompt to explain each step is the human-tested form. Maps to one operator per heuristic step plus a code check that the step was done.

source: Renkl (2023) chapter, footnote on structuredness
finding: Well-structured versus ill-structured is better applied to learning content than to whole domains. School math is mostly well-structured, but finding proofs is ill-structured.
numbers: Footnote 1 of the chapter.
limits: Definitional point.
agent_relevance: Classify by task (is there a check, is there an algorithm), not by topic. The mode switch should look at the task.

source: Agarwal et al. (2024) Many-Shot In-Context Learning
finding: Many-shot prompts help, but gains differ by task type. On MATH500 ground-truth ICL rises then falls (peak near 125 shots). Model-written solutions (Reinforced ICL) plateau near 25 shots, about 5% above human solutions, with no big drop.
numbers: MATH500 (Gemini 1.5 Pro): reinforced ICL plateau at ~25 shots, ~5 points above ground-truth ICL; 4-shot Minerva prompt 55.7% MATH500, 90.6% GSM8K. GPQA: degradation at 250 shots. BBH: Reinforced > Unsupervised > human 3-shot CoT; one task 77.1% vs 83%.
limits: Mostly verifiable tasks (math, MCQ, BBH). Little on open generation.
agent_relevance: On verifiable tasks model-made worked examples help. No such evidence for open tasks, so do not carry the math recipe to open mode.

source: Agarwal et al. (2024) Many-Shot ICL, unsupervised ICL result
finding: Problems alone (no solutions) matched or beat problems with solutions on MATH. Where the model already knows the procedure, examples add little. Where outputs define the task, solutions are needed.
numbers: MATH500 and GSM8K transfer: many-shot unsupervised ICL >= ground-truth ICL. Authors: unsupervised ICL may not perform well when outputs are critical for specifying the task (Fig 9, A.11).
quote: it may not perform well, for example, when outputs are critical for specifying the task
limits: Gemini 1.5 Pro only.
agent_relevance: Examples help most when the task spec lives in the example outputs. Open tasks are exactly that case.

source: Min et al. (2022) Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations: What Makes In-Context Learning Work?
finding: Random labels in demonstrations barely hurt on classification and multi-choice. What matters: label space, input distribution, format. Examples act as format and space cues, not taught reasoning.
numbers: 12+ models including GPT-3; classification and multi-choice tasks. EMNLP 2022.
quote: ground truth demonstrations are in fact not required
limits: Closed-form tasks only. Li et al. 2024 show a different pattern on open questions.
agent_relevance: LLM 'worked examples' may not act like human worked examples (schema building). Do not copy CLT claims onto prompts without testing.

source: Li et al. (2024) Why does in-context learning fail sometimes? Evaluating in-context learning on open and closed questions
finding: On hard open-form science questions a MORE relevant context scored LOWER than no context. On closed-form benchmarks relevance helped. Direct evidence that example help flips with task type.
numbers: 160 physics and CS questions; 3 difficulty levels; 3 originality levels (known, paraphrased, original); 4 context types; GPT-4-1106 answers; 6 graders, z-scored. Highest score: no context; lowest: relevant context. Opposite sign on two closed-form sets (MetaICL, NephSAP).
quote: a context that is more aligned with the topic does not always help more than a less relevant context
limits: One model (GPT-4), small set, subjective grading. Authors call it counter-intuitive and do not fully explain it.
agent_relevance: On open problems a close example may anchor the model and hurt. Open mode should not stuff in near-match examples by default.

source: Sprague et al. (2025) To CoT or not to CoT? Chain-of-thought helps mainly on math and symbolic reasoning (ICLR 2025)
finding: Meta-analysis of 100+ papers plus own tests (20 datasets, 14 models): CoT helps mainly on math, symbolic and logic. Little on commonsense, knowledge, soft reasoning. Task type decides.
numbers: Mean CoT gain: symbolic 14.2, math 12.3, logic 6.9 points. Top 3 categories: 56.9 with CoT vs 45.5 without. All other categories: 56.8 vs 56.1. MATH gain up to 41.6, GSM8K up to 66.9 points. Few-shot vs zero-shot CoT: little difference.
quote: CoT gives strong performance benefits primarily on tasks involving math or logic, with much smaller gains on other types of tasks
limits: Mostly single-answer benchmarks. Real open tasks barely measured.
agent_relevance: Step-by-step scaffolds suit the verifiable side and are weak for soft tasks. Pick the mode by task type in code, not by model opinion.

source: Sprague et al. (2025) To CoT or not to CoT, symbolic-solver comparison
finding: CoT gains on MMLU appear only when the question or answer contains an equals sign. CoT beats direct answering at execution but loses to a symbolic solver or tool.
numbers: MMLU: near-identical accuracy with and without CoT unless '=' present. Plan+Tool solver beat Plan+CoT solver on average across models.
limits: Tool route needs a formal task; CommonsenseQA cannot be formalised.
agent_relevance: Where a check or tool exists, use code. Where none exists (open tasks), written reasoning alone gives small gains.

source: Stechly, Valmeekam & Kambhampati (2025) Chain of Thoughtlessness? An Analysis of CoT in Planning
finding: Worked-step prompts in Blocksworld helped only when the example class matched the test class closely. General algorithm demos helped less, and gains died as stack size grew. Examples taught pattern match, not a general procedure.
numbers: Table-to-stack, 261 instances. GPT-4: zero-shot 3.83%, general n-shot 6.13%, universal-algorithm CoT 51.3%, stacking-specific CoT 59.3%. Claude-3-Opus: 9.96% zero-shot, 24.5% stacking CoT. GPT-4-Turbo: 19.1% zero-shot, 40.6% stacking CoT. Self-consistency lowered scores.
quote: we only find meaningful performance improvements from chain of thought prompts when those prompts are exceedingly specific to their problem class
limits: Old models; well-structured planning. Newer reasoning models not tested here.
agent_relevance: Even in a well-structured domain example benefit is narrow. In open mode examples are less likely to transfer.

source: Stechly et al. (2025) Chain of Thoughtlessness, synthetic scalable domains
finding: Authors built scalable variants of three domains common in CoT papers and found the same failure: gains fall once problems grow beyond the example size.
numbers: Section 6 extension; main numbers in Table 1 (see c11).
limits: I read only the Blocksworld table closely.
agent_relevance: Test any example-based helper at sizes beyond the example size before trusting it.

source: Upasani et al. (2026) Test-time adaptation via many-shot prompting: benefits, limits, and pitfalls (ICLR 2026)
finding: Many-shot prompting works for structured tasks with high information gain (extraction, constrained output). It gives small gains on open-ended generation (translation). Selection strategy matters and more shots can hurt.
numbers: Llama-3.3-70B and Llama-3.1-8B. Banking77 label-similarity selection: 83.4% at 1 shot per class down to 67.4% at 70 per class. Shuffle order shifts accuracy 2-3 points. 70B drops at the largest update. WMT16 gains 'consistent but small'. 5390 demonstrations reach the 128k context limit.
quote: many-shot prompting is effective for structured tasks where demonstrations provide high information gain
limits: Open-source Llama only; the open-ended proxy is translation, which is partly structured.
agent_relevance: 2026 evidence for this subfield's claim: examples fit structured tasks; open tasks need something else. More examples can reduce accuracy.

source: Li et al. (2026) Cognitive Foundations for Reasoning and Their Manifestation in LLMs (arXiv 2511.16660)
finding: 192K model traces (18 models) and 1,346 human think-aloud traces on problems from well- to ill-structured. Both humans and models use fewer reasoning elements on ill-structured problems. Models check less where no answer can be recomputed.
numbers: Matched set: 30 problems (10 story, 10 diagnosis, 10 case analysis), 450 model traces. Humans 41% fewer elements on ill-structured vs well-structured; models 26% fewer. Accuracy 62.4% well-structured, 51.7% intermediate, 57.5% ill-structured. Elements predict success 2.4x more in ill-structured types (PPMI .217 vs .091).
limits: Ill-structured problems are almost all text (539 text vs 9 image, 9 audio). Judge is GPT-4.1.
agent_relevance: Open mode needs structure that models do not supply, especially self-monitoring. Code should force a monitor step where no check exists.

source: Li et al. (2026) Cognitive Foundations, test-time reasoning guidance
finding: Scaffolding the reasoning order seen in successful traces helped most on ill-structured problems, and only for strong models. Weak models lost accuracy.
numbers: All models: +4.4 (SE 1.2) ill-structured vs +1.6 (1.1) well-structured. High-capability: +9.7 (1.8) ill-structured, dilemmas +18.8 (3.7), case analysis +8.4 (2.8), well-structured +5.9 (1.6). High-capability overall 59.0% to 64.3%; mid +1.0; low -3.6 (DeepScaleR-1.5B -13.1, R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B -9.5).
quote: Following a multi-phase reasoning plan while solving the problem is itself demanding
limits: Prompt-level plan, LLM-judged. Model set limited.
agent_relevance: A concrete form of 'other support' for open tasks: a short ordered topology (isolate positions, generate resolutions, trace consequences). Gate it by model capability.

source: Li et al. (2026) Cognitive Foundations, begin-before-representing finding
finding: Models most often begin building a solution before representing the problem. Successful topologies begin with selective attention; typical traces begin with forward chaining.
numbers: Figure 8 topologies for algorithmic and diagnosis problems.
limits: Descriptive; causal test only via the guidance experiment.
agent_relevance: Add a restate-and-select-what-matters slot before open-mode search (fits S0 framing).

source: Yun et al. (2025) The Price of Format: Diversity Collapse in LLMs
finding: The chat template itself collapses diversity on open-ended generation, even at high temperature. Minimal formatting gave the most varied outputs.
numbers: 1024 'random news' headlines: simple prompt spreads across topics; full chat template gives mostly Science. Semantic diversity lower under full template for all tested models and sizes; persists at p=0.9 sampling.
quote: diversity collapse persists even under high-temperature sampling
limits: Small open models (Llama, Qwen3-0.6B/4B, Phi). Measured diversity, not quality.
agent_relevance: Open-mode prompts should be lightly formatted and varied. Rigid scaffold wording can narrow search.

source: Yun et al. (2025) Price of Format, task split
finding: Format consistency matters for structure-sensitive tasks (GSM8K, IFEval) but little for knowledge tasks (MMLU, WebQuestions). Open generation reacts to structural tokens.
numbers: Abstract-level split across task score, alignment, diversity.
limits: Fine-tuning study on small models.
agent_relevance: Strict format suits closed tasks and costs diversity on open tasks: two modes, two prompt styles.

source: Zhang et al. (2026) Verbalized Sampling: How to Mitigate Mode Collapse and Unlock LLM Diversity (arXiv 2510.01171 v4)
finding: Asking for several answers with stated probabilities restores diversity on creative tasks without training. Bigger models gain more.
numbers: Creative writing diversity 1.6-2.1x over direct prompting; human evaluation +25.7%; recovers 66.8% of base-model diversity; GPT-4.1 and Gemini-2.5-Pro gain 1.5-2x more than mini/flash. Quality stays comparable.
quote: Generate 5 jokes about coffee and their corresponding probabilities
limits: Verbalized probabilities are not calibrated. Tasks: poems, stories, jokes, dialogue, synthetic data.
agent_relevance: A cheap open-mode move: ask for N distinct candidates in one call, then let code select (G5). One model asked for a spread, not persona voting (G4).

source: Wadinambiarachchi et al. (2024) The Effects of Generative AI on Design Fixation and Divergent Thinking (CHI 2024)
finding: Human study with AI images as example source in a creative sketching task. Midjourney images raised fixation on the first example and lowered fluency, variety and originality versus no support.
numbers: N=60 between-participants; 3 conditions (none, Google Image Search, Midjourney). GenAI fixation +0.32 (89% CI .11-.55), BF 124; fluency estimate -0.21; variety -0.15 (BF 2.64, anecdotal); originality -0.03 (89% CI -.06 to .00).
limits: Visual ideation; modest effects. Humans, not LLMs, but AI-made examples.
agent_relevance: Why examples can hurt creative work: fixation on the shown idea. Open mode should delay, rotate or contrast examples.

source: Lin et al. (2026) Heuristic Classification of Thoughts prompting (HCoT, arXiv 2604.12390)
finding: Expert-system heuristic classification (abstract the case, match a pre-listed solution pattern, refine) used inside an LLM loop for ill-structured inductive tasks. Gains are modest: on 24 Game it is cheaper than ToT but less accurate; on 1D-ARC it roughly ties plain prompts.
numbers: 24 Game, 1362 items: IO 5.65%, CoT 9.54%, ToT-prompt 3.16%, ToT-BFS 55.65% (7.28M generated tokens), best HCoT 36.49% (2.88M tokens). 1D-ARC, 901 items, GPT-4o: IO 44.06%, ToT-prompt 47.61%, HCoT 40.06%; stronger model: IO 82.91%, Auto-CoT 85.90%, best 87.46%, HCoT 85.46%. 16 patterns (24.3%) worse than 6 (32.53%).
limits: Abstract claims HCoT beats ToT/CoT on ill-structured tasks; the tables show mixed results and ceiling effects. Pattern lists are hand-built. I did not map every row of the 1D-ARC table to its model label.
agent_relevance: A hand-built pattern library is a possible open-mode support. Too many patterns add noise; keep the list short.

source: Bichler et al. (2022) Learning to solve ill-defined statistics problems: does self-explanation quality mediate the worked example effect? (Instructional Science)
finding: Not read beyond the title and abstract head this session. It tests whether self-explanation quality mediates the worked example effect on ill-defined statistics problems.
numbers: Not read.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Candidate for the human boundary-condition pass.

source: Marsh, Landau & Hicks (1996) How examples may (and may not) constrain creativity (Memory & Cognition)
finding: Not read beyond the title and first lines this session. Three experiments on whether ideas conform to examples shown in a creative generation task.
numbers: Not read.
limits: Not opened.
agent_relevance: Candidate link to fixation and conformity for open-mode example design.

source: Agarwal et al. (2024) Many-Shot ICL, ordering and loss
finding: Example order changes MATH results a lot. Next-token loss on solutions does not predict downstream accuracy, and accuracy on MATH and GPQA falls after ~125 shots.
numbers: Ten random orderings of fixed 50 MATH examples gave clearly different test accuracy (Fig 17). Success rate on MATH and GPQA decreases after 125 shots while NLL keeps falling (Figs 7, 8, 18).
limits: Gemini 1.5 Pro; verifiable tasks.
agent_relevance: Example-based help is fragile. Any example slot needs held-out checks (G3), not trust in model likelihood.
